name: Facade-Brine
geological_features: Deep freshwater ocean beneath saline layer
specific_features: Stratified ocean with distinct saline and freshwater layers supporting different ecosystems
description: Facade-Brine is an oceanic world with a unique hydrological structure: a shallow, hypersaline upper ocean sitting atop a deep freshwater ocean, the two layers separated by a density boundary so sharp it is visible to the naked eye when diving. The scattered landmasses are ringed by salt-encrusted cliff facades that glitter white in the sunlight, their surfaces carved into intricate patterns by the dual tides of the two ocean layers. Tidal salt flats extend for kilometers at low water, their crystalline surfaces crunching underfoot.

The atmosphere is breathable and carries the sharp, clean scent of salt. The visual effect of the dual ocean is remarkable: the upper layer is pale turquoise, the lower layer a deep indigo visible through the boundary in calm conditions. From the cliff tops, the ocean appears to be two separate bodies of water occupying the same space. The salt facades of the coastlines catch the light at every angle, creating a landscape that seems to be made of polished stone.

The stratified ocean supports two largely independent ecosystems: a salt-tolerant biome in the upper layer and a freshwater biome in the depths. The density boundary acts as an ecological barrier, with very few species crossing between layers. The separation has persisted for at least fifty million years, long enough for significant evolutionary divergence. Some parallel evolution has occurred, with similar body plans appearing independently in both layers.

Facade-Brine's dual ecosystem makes it a treasure for comparative biology, offering a natural experiment in parallel evolution. The medicinal compounds from the saline layer organisms are chemically distinct from those in the freshwater layer, doubling the pharmaceutical potential. Research stations operate on several of the larger landmasses, and the planet has been designated a protected biosphere with limited harvesting permits.
